assessment_scope: Current snapshot for all six filter-response records at registry 0.2.3 after the four-record target-use evidence spike. The four original records are mechanically reassessed; low shelf and high shelf are reproduced unchanged. No record status, semantic field, alias, or artwork changes.

semantic_stability.basis: EV-003 and EV-018 establish high-pass semantics, while current vendor usage documents both High-pass and Low Cut treatments. DA-003 shows that Low Cut is used for high-pass behavior but does not establish exact equivalence in every intended context; EV-024 preserves terminology divergence.

artifact_refs.claim: Supports the observed High-pass and Low Cut terminology treatments without resolving a universal exact-alias rule.

limitations: The exact Low Cut alias boundary remains material and open.

independent_usage.basis: EV-002, EV-100, and EV-101 directly document three independent axis-less target implementations. Independent vendor, implementation, education, trade-media, and community sources exceed five groups across at least three sectors.

artifact_refs.claim: Classifies current vendor representations and prevents contextual controls from being over-counted as axis-less target implementations.
Classifies Image-Line and DSSSP as independent target implementations while preserving publisher-group counting.

limitations: The broad usage corpus does not resolve whether Low Cut is universally exact, nor does implementation use establish portable text interchange.

text_and_accessibility.basis: High-pass filter and HPF are independently and unambiguously used in non-UI education, documentation, and trade prose, grounding the canonical term, fallback, and speech label even though no response glyph is portable plain text.
limitations: EV-023 records user confusion between high-pass and low-pass names; score 3 means actual source use is unambiguous, not that every reader is error-free.

visual_convergence.basis: Ableton EV-002, Image-Line EV-100, and DSSSP EV-101 independently converge on an axis-less monotonic high-pass primitive while differing in curvature, continuation treatment, plateau length, and stroke weight.

artifact_refs.claim: Classifies historical evidence as labeled, axis-bearing, or embedded context rather than standalone glyph lineage.
Shows current visual evidence remains contextual and heterogeneous.
Documents three qualifying high-pass implementations and their primitive-level convergence and divergences.

limitations: Convergence does not establish identical outlines, portable Unicode use, artwork reuse rights, or the exact Low Cut alias boundary.

overlap_audit.basis: DA-005 reproducibly audits Unicode 17 semantic candidates, visual near-misses, plausible sequences, and IEC 60617 terminology using the registered primary inputs, and records explicit non-equivalence and exclusions.

artifact_refs.claim: Supplies the complete reproducible overlap and confusability audit required for score 3.

limitations: The audit excludes later Unicode versions, restricted IEC sheets, IEC 60417, ISO 7000, and font-by-font behavior.

legal_provenance.basis: Every cited ledger source has a rights note, no third-party artwork is imported, and the repository publishes no claimed reference artwork asset.

counterevidence.description: Current and historical sources often communicate the concept with text, axes, or rich UI context rather than a standalone glyph.

artifact_refs.claim: Preserves negative historical findings.
Preserves current representation heterogeneity.

counterevidence.description: Family-level text workarounds do not establish the project's three-example per-record Unicode safeguard.

artifact_refs.claim: Records the bounded plain-text and workaround search result.

material_open_questions.description: Whether Low Cut is an exact alias of high-pass filter across the intended corpus.

artifact_refs.claim: Documents divergent terminology treatments without resolving universal equivalence.

hard_blockers.description: The exact alias boundary between High-pass filter and Low Cut remains unresolved.

artifact_refs.claim: Supports retaining the unresolved alias boundary as a blocker.

failed_requirements: A material alias question and hard blocker remain open.
result.rationale: The score rises from 14 to 18 because three independent axis-less target implementations satisfy maximal usage and visual-convergence evidence. The unresolved Low Cut alias boundary keeps semantic stability below the candidate floor and blocks promotion.

limitations: The stable semantic record does not imply a mandatory glyph contour.

result.rationale: The score rises from 13 to 18 because two independent axis-less target implementations satisfy maximal independent usage and the visual-convergence floor. Independent adverse review passed and the earlier material target-existence question is closed, so the assessment is candidate-eligible. The live record remains evidence-collecting because this bounded spike makes no status change.

semantic_stability.basis: Band-stop semantics are established, but DA-004 finds concurrent narrow-subtype, exact-synonym, response-region, and product-mode uses of Notch with no universal Q or bandwidth boundary.

artifact_refs.claim: Establishes that Notch remains a context-dependent related term rather than a universally exact alias.

limitations: Notch remains a provisional related term and the material boundary remains open.

independent_usage.basis: Image-Line EV-100 directly documents one axis-less selector labeled Band stop, and EV-003 independently grounds band-stop semantics. DSSSP EV-101 is excluded because its implementation is explicitly Notch and the material boundary remains unresolved.

artifact_refs.claim: Documents Notch and Band-Eliminate representation treatments without proving a band-stop target glyph.
Prevents borrowing Notch implementations as exact band-stop uses.
Counts the explicit Image-Line Band stop selector and excludes DSSSP Notch from band-stop use.

limitations: Only one qualifying target implementation is established. Image-Line mixed wording is product-local and cannot resolve the cross-domain Notch boundary.

text_and_accessibility.basis: Band-stop terminology is source-supported, but the registry's BSF fallback remains ungrounded in this corpus; EV-018 documents BEF instead.
limitations: The drafted BSF fallback is not independently source-grounded.

visual_convergence.basis: EV-100 directly documents one compact axis-less rejected-band selector labeled Band stop. No second qualifying band-stop implementation is established, and Notch-only sources remain excluded.

artifact_refs.claim: Classifies current Notch and Band-Eliminate representations as contextual or semantically non-transferable.
Explains why Notch visual evidence cannot establish band-stop convergence.
Documents one qualifying band-stop target rendering and preserves the Notch exclusion.

limitations: One implementation cannot establish convergence. The Notch boundary and the drafted BSF fallback remain open.

overlap_audit.basis: DA-005 supplies a reproducible semantic-equivalent, visual-confusable, sequence, and adjacent-standard audit, including a separate disposition for the unresolved Notch boundary.

artifact_refs.claim: Supplies the complete overlap audit required for score 3.

limitations: The overlap audit does not resolve the Notch semantic boundary.

legal_provenance.basis: Every cited source has a rights note, no third-party artwork is imported, and no reference artwork asset is published.

counterevidence.description: Authoritative and community sources materially disagree on whether Notch is an exact alias, narrow subtype, central response region, or product mode.

artifact_refs.claim: Preserves all conflicting boundary usages and the absence of a universal threshold.

material_open_questions.description: Whether Notch filter should remain only a related narrow-band case or can be an exact alias in a future interoperable scope.

artifact_refs.claim: Demonstrates that the reviewed corpus cannot settle one universal relationship.

hard_blockers.description: The interoperable semantic boundary between Band-stop and Notch remains unresolved.

artifact_refs.claim: Supports retaining the boundary as a hard blocker.

failed_requirements: Text and accessibility score is below 2.
A material Notch boundary and hard blocker remain open.
result.rationale: The score rises from 10 to 12 because an explicit Image-Line Band stop selector satisfies one target-use level and the usage midpoint. DSSSP Notch is conservatively excluded; the semantic boundary, BSF fallback, and missing second target implementation prevent promotion.

semantic_stability.basis: Independent product, implementation, historical, education, trade, and community sources support a sign-agnostic low-frequency-side shelf concept. Exact alias treatment for low shelving filter remains open.
limitations: Hybrid implementations and the shelf-versus-shelving alias disposition prevent a maximal score.

independent_usage.basis: Multiple independent organizations and authors use low shelf as a filter type across product documentation, an implementation specification, education, trade media, historical documentation, and community discussion. Project reports summarize these sources but are not counted as additional evidence.
limitations: Broad semantic usage does not establish portable glyph usage or one common contour.

text_and_accessibility.basis: The full term low shelf is independently used in education, trade, product, and community prose, supporting LOW SHELF and low-shelf filter without relying on unsupported abbreviations.
limitations: LS and LSF are not established as portable, unambiguous fallbacks.

visual_convergence.basis: EV-052 and EV-054 document compact type selectors, but the evidence does not establish shared axis-less geometry or a reproducible sign-agnostic primitive.
limitations: Contextual product selectors cannot be treated as convergent standalone glyphs or reused as artwork.

overlap_audit.basis: DA-009 reproducibly audits Unicode 17 semantic candidates, lexical false positives, representative smooth-fork visual near-misses, plausible sequences, and ISO/IEC 10646, SMuFL, IEC, and AES adjacency. It records explicit non-equivalence and bounded exclusions for both shelf records.

artifact_refs.claim: Supplies the reproducible shelf-specific semantic-equivalent, visual-confusable, sequence, adjacent-standard, and exclusion audit required for score 3.

limitations: Restricted standards content, exhaustive IEC 60417 and ISO 7000 searching, subscriber-only AES material, font-by-font rendering, and participant recognition remain outside the audit.

legal_provenance.basis: All cited ledger entries record rights limitations, no third-party artwork is imported, and no shelf artwork is accepted or published by this record.

counterevidence.description: Curve orientation alone can describe either low-side boost or high-side attenuation, so the affected side is not recoverable from every unlabelled curve.
Reviewed product, educational, trade, and community sources frequently use labels, controls, contextual curves, or prose rather than a portable standalone shelf glyph.

The bounded record-specific friction search found only one clearly qualifying new artifact for this shelf. Adequate prose and numeric parameters remain material counterevidence, and no portable shelf character, shelf-specific PUA or custom-font use, or hand-drawn exchange was established.

artifact_refs.claim: Preserves the conservative per-record qualification result and excluded findings; the project's three-independent-source friction safeguard remains open.

material_open_questions.description: Whether low shelving filter is an exact alias or should remain a related term.
Whether independent compact implementations converge on a sign-agnostic affected-side primitive distinguishable from high pass.

hard_blockers.description: Cross-vendor compact glyph convergence and six-way shelf/pass recognition are not established.

failed_requirements: Material topology, target-rendering, and shelving-term questions remain open.
The project's three-independent-source plain-text-friction safeguard remains open.
result.rationale: The score rises mechanically from 14 to 17 because DA-009 completes the reproducible shelf-specific overlap audit. DA-010 preserves real communication friction but remains below the project's three-source safeguard and does not change the already-grounded text/accessibility score. Visual convergence and material research questions prevent promotion.
